newsitem.title: USA: Ralph Lauren shares jump 25 percent at opening.
newsitem.headline: Ralph Lauren shares jump 25 percent at opening.

text.p: Shares of Polo Ralph Lauren Corp RL.N jumped 25 percent at the opening of trading on Tuesday after the initial public offering of the design firm.
Shares jumped 6-1/2 to 32-1/2. Lauren, a former necktie salesman from the Bronx, rang the opening bell to signal the start of the trading session at the exchange.

Some analysts while the stock might have an initial rise, it could trade lower as investors "flip" the stock for short-term gains. They said with so much interest from the retail industry, a lot of stock was taken away that otherwise would have gone to institutional investors.
"Institutions got very small allocations based on a 30 million share deal. That's a negative. I'm bailing out now," said one trader.
Institutions generally hold stocks as a long-term investment, providing the strong hands a deal needs during rough periods when smaller investors might sell.
"I'm very disappointed and even annoyed. I got nothing and I put in for a lot and I put in early," said Peggy Farley, chief executive of Amas Securities.

Not everyone went empty-handed. Arden Armstrong, a portfolio manager at Miller Anderson & Sherrerd LLP, a Conshohocken, Pa.-based fund that manages more than $41 billion, said she got a 250,000 share allocation.

"This is a very strong company with a great brand name, international growth opportunities and a very diversified product line, so they don't have the same 'fashion risk' as some other designers," she said.
She also although she expects flat operating margins in Polo's menswear business in 1997, she expects them to grow in 1998 and beyond after the company revamps the unit.
Revenues at Ralph Lauren have gone from $846.6 million in fiscal 1995 to $1.18 billion in fiscal 1997 and earnings have increased from $80.2 million to $117.3 million.
But Alan Millstein, editor and publisher of the Fashion Report, warned about betting on the fashion industry.

"Wall Street never learns. With the exception of Gucci Group NV, which has defied all the odds, and Liz Claiborne Inc, no fashion brand has ever last more than 20 years. It's like betting on a film studio. It may be great at the box office today but you better have great product in the pipeline," he said.

About 29.5 million shares were sold in the offering for $26 each, making it the second-largest IPO this year. Santa Fe International Corp SDC.N holds that record. It raised nearly $1 billion in an IPO on Tuesday.
